item.title: EAFP vs LBYL Python: What's the Difference and When to Use Each?
item.description:
“EAFP vs LBYL Python: What’s the Difference and When to Use Each?”

Python’s philosophy often embraces an approach that prioritizes a “do it first, then handle problems if they arise” mentality. This is encapsulated by the EAFP style. In contrast, the LBYL style is more cautious, advocating for checks and validations before attempting an action. Understanding these paradigms is key to writing more robust and efficient Python code.

EAFP: Forgiveness Over Foresight

EAFP is a Pythonic idiom that assumes the existence of necessary keys, attributes, or conditions and directly attempts an operation. If the operation fails due to a missing element or invalid state, it gracefully handles the resulting exception. This style is characterized by the liberal use of try and except blocks.
